artifacts.summary: Codebase research grounding the /slice build: the shared overlay/commit-tree/CAS primitive in review-stack-prepare.sh (not its basis), command-file and suite/manifest registration conventions, the orchestrator-runtime-files.md row precedent for the series file, and a re-measured 412-commit live difference confirming the VERIFY BY precondition.

memory_candidates.content: In agent-system/extensions/core, scripts/review-stack-prepare.sh's rsp_overlay_tree (private GIT_INDEX_FILE + read-tree + per-path update-index --cacheinfo/--force-remove + write-tree) is the canonical worked example of the 'private index overlay' git-plumbing idiom documented generically in context/patterns/ref-plumbing-landing.md. A new script needing the same idiom should re-derive it fresh rather than source/depend on review-stack-prepare.sh when that script is itself scheduled for deletion by another record -- check decision records under specs/decisions/ for a scheduled-deletion status before treating any existing script as a dependency.

In this repository's agent-system source store, commands/tag.md and commands/merge.md are the two reference shapes for user-only command files: /tag (no allowed-tools, narrative workflow, delegates to a skill) for a command with no interactive AskUserQuestion prompts and no direct forge call; /merge (allowed-tools: Bash(git:*), Bash(gh:*), Bash(glab:*), AskUserQuestion) for a command that both prompts interactively and calls the forge CLI directly from the command body rather than from a backing script. Choose the template by whether the new command needs interactive prompts + forge calls, not just by 'is it user-only'.

context/standards/orchestrator-runtime-files.md classifies specs/.orchestration/reviews/<stack id>/manifest.json as 'Durable provenance, but untracked', covered by the pre-existing **/.orchestration/ gitignore directory-class pattern with no new gitignore pattern needed. Any new state file placed under specs/.orchestration/** inherits this gitignore coverage automatically; the only remaining decision is whether it earns its own documentation row in that standards file, which is a discoverability judgment call, not a mechanical requirement.
